phases.name: Anchor LinkedIn extraction on the job link, not block position, to stop silent title/company/location shift

steps.name: Regression test pinning the header-shift defect (RED)
criteria: A block containing two job cards yields two rows, not one — the trailing card is no longer dropped.
Fixture 1a05bf0e7d2000d8 (preamble) yields the true title/company/location triple, not the preamble text, for its job.
Fixture 1a05c5fb49972c37 (raw HTML + Manage alerts + other-alerts header) yields correct triples for both its primary and cross-sell cards.
Fixture 1a09be37fadab08b (alert-created confirmation) yields the real title/company/location, not the confirmation sentences.
Fixture 1a067f6097dc5f98 (Edit alert + token lines) yields the correct triple with location no longer lost.
steps.scenario_name: a block with an unfiltered preamble line no longer shifts the extracted title/company/location triple
steps.implementation_notes: Fixtures MUST be copied byte-for-byte from real cached messages (.cache/messages/2026-09/*.json, gitignored) — never hand-written; this project already had one incident (DR-0007) caused by an invented test model. Commit copies to fixtures/linkedin/, redacting any toRecipients field to me@example.invalid the way fixtures/spill/ already does. Named real examples to copy: 1a05bf0e7d2000d8 (preamble), 1a05c5fb49972c37 (raw HTML + Manage alerts: + other-alerts header), 1a09be37fadab08b (alert-created confirmation, two preamble lines), 1a067f6097dc5f98 (Edit alert + token lines). This test MUST fail against the current shipped parser — confirm RED before handing off to 01-02. Root cause: docs/feature/fix-linkedin-header-shift/rca.md (positional "first three non-noise lines" rule, no structural anchor). TEST PARADIGM: this is a regression/golden-fixture test against real captured messages, not a property — EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: fixture-anchored extraction defect, not a quantifiable invariant over generated input. Compensate with the existing property-style boundary coverage already in coverage.test.mjs at the adjacent core-module level. PATH CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-09-14): regression fixtures go to fixtures/linkedin-variants/, NOT fixtures/linkedin/. The walking-skeleton acceptance test scans fixtures/linkedin/ directory-wide via json-message-reader readAll() and asserts row counts against it, so adding files there drops it to 7/8. Keeping the corpora separate preserves that test without weakening any assertion.

steps.name: Anchor-on-link extraction fix (GREEN)
criteria: Extraction anchors on each `/jobs/view/{id}` occurrence per block, walking backward past trailing noise to take the last three lines as title/company/location.
Every job link in a multi-card block produces its own row; no card is silently dropped.
All five existing fixtures/linkedin fixtures still produce their previously-passing title/company/location values unchanged.
Subject-line salary attaches only to the first extracted job of a message; canonical `/jobs/view/{id}/` link reconstruction is preserved.
tests/regression/job-alert-harvester/linkedin-block-anchor.test.mjs and the existing 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both pass.
steps.scenario_name: a block with an unfiltered preamble line no longer shifts the extracted title/company/location triple
steps.implementation_notes: Approved direction (user decision 2026-09-14, rca.md § Proposed Fix): locate every `View job:` line per block, walk backward past the closed trailing-noise set (This company is actively hiring / Apply with resume & profile / N connection(s) / N company alumni / N school alumni / Promoted / Easy Apply / Actively recruiting / blank lines), take the next three lines as [location, company, title] reversed. linkedin:{jobId} dedup keys come from the URL match, independent of the triple, so a full re-parse of the cache repairs history without changing keys — the repair path DR-0001 (persist what cannot be re-derived) exists for exactly this. Hard constraints: Node 22, ESM, Vitest; dependencies are xlsx and vitest only, no new dependency; src/core/ stays pure — no classes, no mutation, no node: imports. Do not widen NOISE_LINE preamble entries; anchoring makes them unnecessary (removing is optional cleanup, not required here).

steps.name: Close the trailing-noise set over singular alum counts (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job card whose trailing noise reads '1 company alum' or '1 school alum' (singular) extracts the same title/company/location triple as the plural 'N company alumni' form.
The existing plural forms keep matching; no other noise pattern changes.
The full LinkedIn cache corpus yields zero Jobs rows whose Company is a location string and zero whose Location is an alum count.
tests/regression/job-alert-harvester/linkedin-block-anchor.test.mjs and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: a singular alum count is trailing noise, not a meaningful line
steps.implementation_notes: Discovered post-01-02 against the live 59-message cache, not from the original brief. LinkedIn emits '1 company alum' and '1 school alum' in the singular; TRAILING_NOISE_LINE only matches /^\d+ company alumni$/ and /^\d+ school alumni$/, so the singular line counts as meaningful and tripleAbove() shifts the whole triple by one — title takes the company, company takes the location, location takes the alum count. Corpus evidence: 8 occurrences of '1 company alum' and 3 of '1 school alum'; 7 distinct rows wrong, e.g. job 4445955126 yields [Worldpay, 'London Area, United Kingdom', '1 company alum'] where the raw mail reads 'Release Train Engineer' / 'Worldpay' / 'London Area, United Kingdom'. This is the same defect class as 01-02 (an incomplete closed set), not a regression from it. Fix is to make the plural optional in both patterns; do not broaden them beyond alum/alumni.

steps.name: Treat a per-card salary line as trailing noise (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job card carrying a salary line below its location (e.g. '£59K-£78K / year') extracts the same title/company/location triple as a card without one.
The subject-line salary behaviour is unchanged: parseSalaryFromSubject still attaches the subject salary to the headline job only.
The full cache corpus yields zero Jobs rows whose Location starts with '£'.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: a per-card salary line is trailing noise, not the location
steps.implementation_notes: Third instance of the same defect class as 01-02 and 01-03: the trailing-noise set is a denylist and this line was not in it. Corpus evidence: 3 of 198 job cards carry a salary line immediately below the location, e.g. job 4456258182 raw reads 'Senior Scrum Master' / 'Leonardo' / 'Gloucester' / '£59K-£78K / year', and tripleAbove() takes the last three as [£59K-£78K / year, Gloucester, Leonardo], yielding title=Leonardo, company=Gloucester, location=£59K-£78K / year. Add a salary-shaped pattern to TRAILING_NOISE_LINE anchored on a leading £ (optionally preceded by 'up to'); keep it tight enough that it cannot match a company or location. DISCARDING the value is deliberate for this step: capturing per-card salary into Min/Max Salary (annual) is an emerged requirement awaiting a decision, not part of this fix.
